messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a p99 spike for /v1/generate after we enabled spillover routing to the low-cost pool. p50 looks normal.
ashwin: Can you paste the numbers you’re seeing?
maya: Sure — grabbed from last 30m (dashboard rollup):
```
/v1/generate                p50 85ms  p95 120ms p99 420ms
/v1/generate?model=alpha    p50 80ms  p95 115ms p99 400ms
/v1/generate?model=beta     p50 100ms p95 200ms p99 1500ms
```
leo: Beta is the outlier — high tail but low traffic. Are we merging percentiles across routes? The console currently shows a single p99 for the endpoint which looks like it's a merged tdigest.
rachel: AFAIK our telemetry backend does t-digest rollups across shards and we then compute quantiles on the merged digest. That tends to weight by sample count, but small-sample high-tail routes can still be underrepresented in alerts.
maya: Exactly. For users that hit the beta variant it's catastrophic (1500ms p99), but because beta traffic is 2% the global p99 is much lower and barely crosses thresholds.
ashwin: We should decide the signal we want: global merged p99 (what we show today) vs per-route p99 (more actionable for rollouts). Maybe a blended approach.
metrics-bot: Executed query dashboards/query/latency?service=api&agg=tdigest_merge — results cached for 60s :hourglass_flowing_sand:
leo: Proposal: add a "percentile mode" toggle in the console with options: global | weighted_by_count | per_route_max.
- global = merge t-digests across routes
- weighted_by_count = compute quantile across route pcts weighted by request counts
- per_route_max = show the worst route p99 (for safety)
rachel: weighted_by_count is closer to what customers think of as their typical user experience. But note: our sampling scheme (1/1000 events for histograms) makes small routes noisy.
maya: UX idea: default to weighted_by_count, but show a compact per-route distribution (top 5 contributing routes) inline — sparkline + p50/p95/p99 columns + "open details" to expand.
ashwin: Implementation notes: we can either (A) store per-route pre-aggregated p50/p95/p99 hourly (cheap), or (B) increase per-route histogram sampling and keep tdigest for exact merge (expensive). Storage delta matters.
leo: Storage/ingest constraints mean (A) wins. Store hourly pctl snapshot for any route with >X requests, and for low-traffic routes store only p50/p95/p99 when a rollout flag is on.
rachel: API change required: add query param ?percentile_mode=global|weighted|per_route_max and a per-route-breakdown=true flag for console requests. Need contract for clients.
maya: I'll draft an RFC: outline telemetry changes, dashboard UI, and rollout UX (per-variant toggles). Also include a small example of the query we'd run server-side: 
```
SELECT route, approx_quantile(latency_ms, 0.99) AS p99, count(*) AS n
FROM telemetry.requests_hourly
WHERE service='api' AND ts >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY route
ORDER BY p99 DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
(this gives per-route p99 snapshot to compute weighted or max)
ashwin: I'll run a quick simulation comparing tdigest_merge vs weighted_quantile and post results. early heads-up: tdigest_merge underestimates max-route tail when a rare route has huge tail — no surprise. :thinking:
leo: We should also add an alerting tag: "percentile_mode" to make sure SRE alerts use the desired aggregation (we don't want an oncall paging on global p99 when a single low-traffic route is blowing up prod for a small subset of customers).
rachel: Edge-case: what about routes that are split by model variant, region, and customer bucket? The console should let you pivot (variant/region/customer) and maintain the same percentile_mode semantics.
maya: Agreed. I'll include that in RFC and add an example UI mock for rollouts: a variant toggle with inline per-variant p99 and a pill showing which variant contributes most to tail. :eyes:
ashwin: Filed quick pastebin of sim: https://paste.example/sim1234 — shows numeric delta. I’ll follow up with a PR for the telemetry snapshot export.
maya: Thanks — assigning RFC to me. @ashwin please add sim results + test vectors for tdigest vs weighted quantile. We should have unit tests that assert behavior on synthetic distributions.
leo: SGTM. Small follow-ups: add a console flag for engineers to switch percentile_mode in-query for debugging. That will help triage rollouts faster.
maya: Cool — I'll schedule a short sync if anyone wants to walk through the RFC tomorrow. End thread unless objections. :thumbsup:
